standard_prerequisites.name: Derived category of a dg algebra
standard_prerequisites.statement: The localisation of the homotopy category of dg modules at quasi-isomorphisms, with morphisms computed as a derived Hom.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the category in which direct sums and products are asserted to exist (source lines 2896-2904, 2906-2935).

standard_prerequisites.name: Direct sums and products of dg modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: The degreewise direct sum and product of a family of dg modules, with the induced differentials, and their universal properties.
standard_prerequisites.use: The candidates are the levelwise constructions and their universal properties have to be transferred (source lines 2906-2948).

standard_prerequisites.name: Derived Hom and quasi-isomorphism invariance
standard_prerequisites.statement: Morphisms in the derived category are computed by the derived Hom, which only depends on quasi-isomorphism classes (the author's lemma lemma-hom-derived, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what allows the universal property to be checked up to quasi-isomorphism (source lines 2910-2947).

core_obligations: Build the candidate direct sum: take the degreewise direct sum of the family of dg modules and show that it satisfies the universal property of a direct sum in the derived category, using the computation of morphisms by the derived Hom (source lines 2906-2935).

Build the candidate product: take the degreewise product and verify the dual universal property in the derived category, which requires using that morphisms are computed up to quasi-isomorphism (source lines 2935-2948).
Conclude existence: deduce that the derived category has direct sums and products and that the levelwise constructions compute them, as stated (source lines 2948-2949).

proof_roadmap.step: Show the levelwise direct sum satisfies the universal property in the derived category.
Show the levelwise product satisfies the dual universal property.
Conclude the existence of direct sums and products.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-derived-products at source lines 2894-2904: the derived category of a dg algebra has both direct sums and products, and they are computed by taking the corresponding operations on dg modules. The proof at source lines 2906-2950 is an explicit verification that the levelwise constructions satisfy the universal properties in the derived category. It builds the candidate direct sum of a family of dg modules, checks that it satisfies the universal property up to quasi-isomorphism using the description of morphisms in the derived category supplied by the author's computation of the derived Hom, and then repeats the argument in the opposite direction for products, which requires care with the variance of the constructions and with the fact that a product in the derived category is not simply computed degreewise without accounting for quasi-isomorphisms. Recognising which universal property has to be checked in which category is the substance, and the statement lists only the conclusions.
